podcast.body: Nora Jones wrote this song one night after her mom sent her an old guitar from Texas. She had initially known only two chords on the guitar, then learned five, finding the simpler chords more conducive to songwriting than the complex jazz chords she knew on piano. This song was one of the first original compositions she performed publicly during early gigs with Jesse Harris and Lee Alexander at The Living Room. "I learned five chords and I wrote, come away with me one night."

podcast.body: Norah Jones wrote this song in high school, after her college days. She composed it in her tiny bedroom after seeing her friends play, using the five chords she knew. Being a "theory nerd" from second grade piano lessons, she notated the chord changes (e.g., "one, two, three, one, six, five, three, one") in her notebook, but without a voice recorder or cell phone, she forgot the original version by the next morning. "And I didn't have a voice recorder or anything. We didn't have cell phones yet. So I wrote it in my notebook and I wrote the chord changes above it."
